correctness.rationale: At a root w, any u with wRu and R(u)={w} either refutes the antecedent or witnesses the consequent, according to the truth value at w. Conversely, set p true only at w. Symmetry makes the antecedent true and the consequent true exactly if there is such a u; an isolated root fails because the antecedent is vacuous and the consequent false. No finiteness is needed. At a witness u in a globally validating frame, w is the only possible return witness, forcing R(w)={u}; this gives involution components including singleton loops. Pairing exactly 2j labels gives the involution counts. A constant-across-endpoints valuation on a two-cycle simulates each loop valuation, and evaluating both modalities at the unique partner gives the two-endpoint Boolean translation. Fixing r putative leaves forces their root edges and forbids r(n−2)−binom(r,2) other edges, leaving binom(n−r,2) free edges. This proves both exact inclusion-exclusion sums. The resulting ordered-tuple moments converge to (ce^(−c))^r for every fixed r; Poisson moment determinacy yields convergence in law, which at the event threshold 1/2 gives the stated positive-count limit. Its sole optimum is c=1, without a claim about finite-n optimizers. Independent bounded checks tested direct valuations on 1098 symmetric frames and rooted graph counts through n=6 (0,1,3,19,215,4551; python3 /workspace/evidence/review_checks.py 5); the proofs establish the unbounded claims.

evidence: Under symmetry a local witness is the adjacent reverse singleton R(u)={w}; in loop-free graphs it is exactly a degree-one neighbor of the root. Chen–Ma show that a successor of successor-set size at most one is not by itself a local correspondent over weakly transitive frames.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Symmetry supplies the return to w used in the pointwise argument. The earlier weakly transitive correspondence is not this statement and cannot be applied to symmetric non-weakly-transitive examples such as the path on four vertices.

value.rationale: A natural frame restriction collapses a difficult universal-valuation property to a pointwise first-order test, with a complete global structural classification and a two-world test frame. Interpreting the test as a pendant-neighbor event gives exact rooted incidence and a nonmonotone, sharply maximized sparse validity profile. The value is in this logical and probabilistic connection, not new involution numbers or a new Poisson approximation technique.
